summary: Measured CPU/device dispatch with host working-set admission, exact source plans and one routing description
implementation_scope: Host placement, measured capacity-bounded prefix splits with immutable calibration identities and exact-count timing medians, and mixed-source plans; one Routing description (softmax/sigmoid before or after selection, selection-only correction bias, grouped top-k, renormalization, scaling) with its host reference and config mapping. Device router and shared-expert kernels are engine supplied (fused MoE kernels through Kernels) and are checked against the host reference. Timing collection, allocation and routed-expert arithmetic remain external. Optional exact-identity HostMemoryCosts account for CPU scratch, loader bytes, pinned staging and additional file pages on CPU and upload paths; injected admission gates ranking and can be revalidated before allocation.

agent_guidance.use_when: Compare placement or mixed-source dispatch, select CPU/device splits from measured workload-specific costs, or describe a model's router once for host reference and device kernel
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Dispatch adds no useful choice; measured lane curves require comparable work geometry and explicit overlap, otherwise measure whole candidate implementations

Occurrence-preserving split dispatch and weighted contribution combination
Measured CPU/upload/device cost curves, exact identity checks and byte/occurrence-bounded prefix split ranking without interpolation
Deduplicated exact miss demands, protected-source plan validation and one quantize/project handoff
One routing description, its host reference and a fail-closed mapping from Core's parsed config fields
Per-candidate anonymous/pinned/file working-set costs and admission reasons; fresh admission revalidation before submission
engine_supplies: Validated encoded device views, the model's Routing (reference-code defaults, scoring order and correction-bias tensor), routed-expert arithmetic, model-specific shared gating and physical placement
Protected READY snapshot plus complete scratch staging before reads
Exact fallback execution, receipts and measured strategy selection
Matched current model/layout/workload/code/topology identities, measured lane and common-overhead samples under representative contention, valid dual-path misses and protected resident sources
Disjoint incremental peak costs and fresh OS observations, independent device reservations, allocation failure cleanup and an admitted exact fallback
preserve: Every occurrence keeps its expert identity, position and weight
Repeated experts share compatible sources; scratch cannot alias READY content
Overflow uses exact fallback rather than wrapping expert IDs
Miss substitution and gate reweighting are outside this exact dispatch contract and require separate consumer quality criteria
Routing ties select the lower original expert ID and group index; the correction bias changes selection only; shared-down output is unweighted and kept separate from routed contributions
Never rank an unmeasured split as zero cost; deduplicate bundle uploads while retaining every weighted route occurrence; calibration identities must match
Missing memory estimates cannot win; file-backed working sets are not automatically charged as anonymous commit; admission snapshots do not reserve memory

Host/device routing, staging and kernel fusion

code_files.purpose: Executable host placement and source-selection algorithms; optimized quantization, projection and staging are explicit backend hooks
Immutable sample curves and identities; measured prefix dispatch planning with exact routes, unique uploads, explicit overlap and capacity/missing-data handling
Routing description, its host reference for one token and the mapping from Core's parsed config fields

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ and standard library for the host reference; backend hardware is an engine choice
requires.model: Expert-routed execution with explicit route occurrences and compatible source representations
requires.workload: Memory-constrained placement or mixed-source routed projections; fixed/scratch capacities use different units

contract.input: Ordered routing occurrences; protected READY slot/generation snapshot, explicit capacity and disjoint scratch; static allocation groups and fixed/workspace/headroom byte extents; routing takes logits, top-k, a Routing and an optional correction bias; measured planning also takes current calibration identity, raw timing curves, complete upload extents and staging/route limits; optional HostMemoryCosts with exact route/upload tables and an injected admission callback
contract.output: Host/device partitions or a single exact cache/scratch/stock plan with deduplicated staging demands; one quantize/project submission through declared hooks; feasible static prefix plans; original expert IDs/weights under the Routing; feasible measured split candidates with missing-sample reasons and an optional best estimate; incremental host memory bytes and admission decisions/reasons retained for each candidate
contract.ownership: Caller retains leases for every source, route buffer, activation and result until completion. READY snapshots do not pin owners; scratch is reserved for the operation.
contract.failure: Reject conflicting/duplicate occurrences, invalid weights, source-slot aliases, unprotected scratch overlap, invalid generations and fabricated demands. Scratch exhaustion preserves original stock expert IDs. Measured planning rejects identity mismatches and invalid samples; absent samples cannot win and no measured feasible plan returns best=None for caller fallback. Missing or rejected memory costs cannot win; failed revalidation requires replanning or exact fallback before allocation/submission.
contract.core_boundary: Consumer owns partition policy/arithmetic; core owns physical services and producer quiescence.

validation.host: Host fixtures and worked example cover budget feasibility, repeated routes, exact fallback, scratch separation and one activation preparation; measured policy fixtures check median/sparse/nonlinear costs, identity changes, explicit overlap, byte and occurrence limits, arbitrary widths, repeated expert uploads and weighted result preservation; RAM/commit/cgroup limits, unknown costs/observations, distinct experts and upload sources, fresh revalidation, zero incremental resident paths and route preservation; routing fixtures check hand-worked cases, the transformers router code of Mixtral, Qwen2/Qwen3-MoE, GPT-OSS, Llama 4, DeepSeek-V2/V3, GLM-4.5, MiniMax-M2, Ernie 4.5 and LongCat-Flash when installed, and the fail-closed config mapping
validation.native: Device routing and shared-expert kernels are engine supplied; compare them with the host Routing reference (routing.py) on the model's parameterization
validation.performance: Unmeasured for a native engine; host fixture success is not a speed claim

native_integration.status: Router and shared-expert kernels, mixed-source routed-expert arithmetic and physical cache staging are engine services
required_hooks: Route-preserving projection arithmetic and physical source/result ownership for the selected path
One quantization and one source-aware projection hook when execute_mixed is selected
Complete scratch-bundle staging before projection reads when scratch is used
Scheduler copies and projection use the same protected READY snapshot/version when caching is used
native_integration.integration_scope: Optional consumer dispatch. Split execution does not require the mixed-source hook or device routing.
optimization_candidates: Choose a unified cache/stock native projection over split execution when duplicate work is a measured bottleneck
Device route resolution without host readback
native_integration.first_native_milestone: Real-layer mixed resident/original projection, exact misses and scheduler copies using the same protected snapshot, with actual backend placement asserted after allocation and activation provenance declared. Then verify full-model decode and source transitions independently; isolated parity or configuration tuning is insufficient.
